results.title: Lambda announces GPU price rises of about 15% — B200, H100 and A100 80GB, from Nov 16 | GPUJournal
highlights:
Nov 6, 2026

Read on Lambda's own pricing page today, Nov 6, 2026: the Instances table now prints the prices that take effect on Nov 16, 2026 — HGX B200 up $1.00 an hour, H100 up $0.60 and A100 80GB up $0.40. It is the largest single announced rise we have caught this autumn, and renters have ten days' notice.

Image: GPUJournal price record — read on lambda.ai/pricing

What was announced, in the pricing page's own words (read Nov 6, 2026): 'These prices take effect November 16, 2026, at 00:00 UTC. Until then, log in to your Lambda Cloud account to see current pricing.' The printed Nov 16 rates: HGX B200 $7.69 an hour (from the $6.69 last verified on Nov 5, +14.9%), HGX H100 $4.59 (from $3.99, +15.0%), HGX A100 80GB $3.19 (from $2.79, +14.3%), and HGX A100 40GB unchanged at $1.99. Lambda is also now at a new address — lambda.com — announced on its blog on Nov 5, 2026; the pricing page itself still answers at lambda.ai/pricing.

How we are treating it: an announced rise is not a live price. Our board keeps Lambda's last verified rates until Nov 16 and will move only when the new rates are re-verified in effect on or after that date — the rise is recorded in Price Watch today as announced, with both dates. One consequence of the announcement is already live, though: Lambda's currently-effective rates can no longer be read on its public page, only after logging in, so today's public check could verify the future rates but not re-read the current ones.

results.title: Linode price increase 2023: Shared and Dedicated plans up 20%
results.author: Fieldnote Labs
highlights:
Akamai raised prices for Linode compute on April 1, 2023, after it bought Linode. Shared CPU and Dedicated CPU plans went up 20%. The 2GB Shared plan went from $10 to $12 a month, and the 4GB plan went from $20 to $24. The $5 Nanode did not change. Extra IPv4 addresses went from $1 to $2 a month, and egress overage fell from $0.01 to $0.005 per GB. We do not track Linode on SaaS Price Watch yet. More vendors are on the vendor list.

...

Shared CPU plans

| Nanode 1GB | $5 a month | $5 a month | no change |
| Linode 2GB | $10 a month | $12 a month | +$2, 20% |
| Linode 4GB | $20 a month | $24 a month | +$4, 20% |
| Linode 8GB | $40 a month | $48 a month | +$8, 20% |

Dedicated CPU plans

| Plan | Old price | New price | Change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Dedicated 4GB | $30 a month | $36 a month | +$6, 20% |
| Dedicated 8GB | $60 a month | $72 a month | +$12, 20% |
| Dedicated 16GB | $120 a month | $144 a month | +$24, 20% |
| Dedicated 32GB | $240 a month | $288 a month | +$48, 20% |

...

## What Akamai said

The Akamai post says: "The price of Shared and Dedicated compute plans will increase by 20%. Our shared Nanode plan remains unchanged at US$5 per month." It adds: "Additional IPv4 IP addresses will increase from US$1 to US$2 per month. IPv6 addresses remain free."

On timing: "The new pricing will go into effect on April 1, 2023."

## Who it hits and when

- Shared CPU and Dedicated CPU customers, new and existing, from April 1, 2023.
- Nanode users saw no change at $5 a month.
- Users with extra IPv4 addresses pay $2 a month per address.
- Users with high egress pay less for overage, $0.005 per GB.
- We do not list High Memory or GPU plans here. The notice did not include them in the increase.

## What to do before your renewal

Linode bills by the hour with a monthly cap, so there is no renewal date. The new price applies to the next bill.

...

When did Linode raise prices? On April 1, 2023. Akamai announced the change on March 1, 2023.

results.title: Linode : hausse des tarifs après le rachat par Akamai
results.author: Patrice Marsollier
highlights:
Les tarifs Linode, désormais commercialisés dans l’offre cloud d’Akamai, vont de 5 $ à 1 152 $ par mois pour les instances à CPU partagé, relevés le 6 février 2026 sur la grille publique Akamai. Le prix affiché inclut l’instance, le stockage local et un quota de trafic, mais exclut les répartiteurs, certains services gérés et les dépassements.

...

- Le Nanode à 5 $ par mois comprend 1 vCPU, 1 Go de mémoire, 25 Go de stockage et 1 To de trafic inclus.
- La facturation est horaire avec un plafond mensuel correspondant au prix de l’instance maintenue tout le mois.
- Le trafic inclus augmente jusqu’à 16 To sur l’offre à 192 $, puis plafonne à 20 To dès le palier à 384 $.
- Un NodeBalancer ajoute 10 $ par mois et son trafic sortant hors forfait est plus cher que celui d’une instance servie directement.
- Le rachat de Linode par Akamai en 2022 a conservé une grille lisible, mais a élargi le nombre de lignes susceptibles d’apparaître sur la facture.

Ces montants concernent les instances Shared CPU de Linode, pour un hébergement professionnel ou un environnement applicatif de petite structure. Les instances à CPU dédié, les GPU, les serveurs bare metal, les remises négociées et les prestations d’exploitation ne sont pas inclus dans ce relevé.

...

La grille des serveurs partagés demeure le point d’entrée le plus simple à lire chez Akamai Cloud Computing. Le tarif dépend d’un palier fixe de processeur virtuel, de mémoire, de stockage SSD et de trafic mensuel. La grille cloud publique d’Akamai, consultée le 6 février 2026, affiche dix paliers allant de 5 $ à 1 152 $ par mois.

La facturation est horaire. Une instance activée quelques heures ne supporte donc pas une mensualité entière. En revanche, une instance active durant tout le cycle de facturation ne dépasse pas le plafond mensuel annoncé. Cette règle est pratique pour provisionner un serveur de test pendant quelques jours, mais elle ne dispense pas de suivre les services annexes, qui obéissent à leur propre grille.

results.title: RunPod Serverless GPU prices are up — B200 up about 25%, every tier higher | GPUJournal
highlights:
RunPod's Serverless GPU rates have risen on every tier, recorded between the Oct 26 and Nov 2, 2026 captures of its own pricing page: B200 $8.64 → $10.79 an hour is the largest move, up about 25%. RunPod announced nothing — the new figures are simply the ones live on runpod.io/pricing today, which we read first-hand on Nov 2.

...

What changed — the new figures read on RunPod's own pricing page (runpod.io/pricing) on Nov 2, 2026, against the figures captured from the same page on Oct 26, 2026: B300 $10.65 → $11.99 (up about 13%), B200 $8.64 → $10.79 (up about 25%), H200 $5.93 → $6.99 (up about 18%), H100 $4.79 → $5.39 (up about 13%), RTX 5090 $1.58 → $1.79 (up about 13%), RTX 4090 $1.10 → $1.34 (up about 22%), and the grouped L4 / A5000 / 3090 rate $0.69 → $0.75 (up about 9%). Every Serverless tier rose; none fell. On sourcing, plainly: the after-figures are RunPod's own page as we read it today; the before-figures are PricingSaaS Pulse's dated Oct 26 capture of that same page, because our own archive does not hold the October Serverless buckets — the comparison is recorded at pricingsaas.com/companies/runpod/diffs/2026W45. There is no RunPod announcement and no stated effective date; the honest date for the change is the window between the two captures.

results.title: AWS vs Azure vs GCP Cloud GPU Pricing [2026]
results.author: Sana Rahman
highlights:
Cloud GPU pricing used to be a simple spreadsheet exercise: look up the hourly rate for an H100 instance, multiply by the hours you need, pick the cheapest provider. In October 2026 that spreadsheet broke. AWS raised its Blackwell B200 Capacity Block rate by roughly 15% on October 7, Microsoft Azure is one of the only major clouds still publishing a flat per-GPU hourly rate for H100 capacity, and Google Cloud has yet to post an official list price for H100, H200 or B200 instances at all. Comparing AWS vs Azure vs GCP cloud GPU pricing now means comparing three different billing philosophies, not just three price tags.

...

What AWS has not done, at least not in any officially confirmed source available as of October 23, 2026, is publish a flat on-demand hourly price for P5, P5e, P5en or P6-B200. Capacity Block pricing is explicitly dynamic, and AWS’s public materials direct buyers to request a quote or check the Capacity Blocks console rather than read a rate card.

...

Azure’s current GPU VM lineup for AI training includes NC40ads H100 v5, ND96isr H100 v5 and ND96isr H200 v5. Two of those SKUs give us the cleanest published numbers in this entire comparison. The NC40ads H100 v5 size, a single-H100 configuration, carried a reported East US pay-as-you-go Linux rate of $6.98 per hour as of October 19, 2026. The larger ND96isr H100 v5 size, which packs eight H100 GPUs, was reported at $98.32 per VM-hour in East US on the same date, which works out to $12.29 per GPU-hour.

Azure also lists an ND96isr H200 v5 size with eight H200 GPUs carrying 141 GB of memory each, making it the newest Hopper-class GPU family Azure has confirmed. Microsoft has not published an officially confirmed Azure B200 virtual machine family or hourly price as of October 23, 2026. Separately, Microsoft Foundry’s managed-compute tier, still in preview, bills hourly per accelerator across A100, H100, H200 and MI300 GPU families, but Microsoft’s documentation says rates vary by accelerator family, region, deployment scope and commitment term, and directs customers to the Azure Pricing Calculator rather than a published table.

...

Google Cloud confirmed on October 2, 2026 that its A3 instance family is powered by Nvidia H100 Tensor Core GPUs, while A3 Ultra instances carry Nvidia H200 Tensor Core GPUs. The newer A4 family, confirmed October 21, 2026, uses Nvidia HGX B200 GPUs, with the a4-highgpu-8g configuration packing eight B200 GPUs per instance. None of these three families has a confirmed, officially published public hourly price in the current research set. Google’s materials mention multiple consumption models for these instances, including on-demand, Spot and committed-use pricing, but do not spell out the specific rates for A3, A3 Ultra or A4.

...

| GPU | AWS (published rate) | Azure (published rate) | Google Cloud (published rate) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| H100, single GPU | No flat rate published; Capacity Blocks price dynamically | $6.98/hour, NC40ads H100 v5, East US, captured Oct. 19, 2026 | Not published |
| H100, 8-GPU node | No flat rate published | $98.32/hour ($12.29/GPU-hour), ND96isr H100 v5, East US, captured Oct. 19, 2026 | Not published |
| H200, 8-GPU node | No flat rate published | No flat on-demand VM rate confirmed in official sources | Not published |
| B200, per GPU-hour (Capacity Block) | $14.208/hour, effective Oct. 7, 2026, up from $12.355/hour (about a 15% increase) | Not offered / not confirmed | Not published; A4 uses Flex-start scheduling instead of a flat rate |

...

## The October 7 AWS B200 Price Hike, Explained

The single clearest pricing move any of the three providers made in the last three months was AWS’s. Effective October 7, 2026, AWS raised its P6-B200 Capacity Block price from $12.355 to $14.208 per accelerator-hour, an increase of approximately 15%, according to GPU-pricing trackers Axis Intelligence and Dev.to’s FastGPU column, which independently captured the same before-and-after figures. For an eight-GPU P6-B200 node, the current instance-hour rate is about $113.666, a noticeable jump in monthly spend for teams running sustained training jobs.

results.title: GPU rental prices in 2026: H100, H200 and B200 per hour
results.author: Safeguard Security Team
highlights:
In October 2026, published on-demand list prices for an H100 ranged from about $2 to about $12 per GPU-hour, depending on the provider, the billing model and what is bundled. Specialist clouds mostly sit between $3 and $6. Spot and long commitments can cut the price by half or more. B200 list prices run from about $6 to $14.

- B200 index price: $2.31 per hour in early March 2026 and $4.95 in late April 2026, per the Ornn Compute Price Index as reported on tomtunguz.com on 27 April 2026.

...

The IntuitionLabs survey says plainly that its entries mix prepaid capacity, on-demand VMs, pods, and cluster and node rates, and are not interchangeable. Its inclusion rule is publicly displayed hourly rates for a matching product, taken from first-party pages, with promotional rates excluded. It is a survey by one publisher, not an official price index, and its method is as the publisher describes it.

...

The large clouds charge the most on-demand. IntuitionLabs lists AWS at $6.88 per GPU-hour for the 8-GPU instance in three US regions and $8.60 in N. California. Azure's own price feed shows $6.98 for a single-GPU VM and $98.32 for the 8-GPU VM in East US, which is $12.29 per GPU. IntuitionLabs lists Google at $11.06 per GPU in Iowa and Oracle at $10.00.

Specialist clouds list lower. ... Runpod's page shows its SXM pod at $3.99 in Secure Cloud and $2.69 in

...

Several of these went up. According to the survey, AWS Capacity Blocks rose from $5.19 to $5.97, Runpod Secure Cloud H100 SXM from $3.29 to $3.99, Lambda's 8-GPU SXM from $2.99 (a 2025 snapshot) to $3.99, and Nebius's HGX H100 from $3.85 to $4.50 effective 1 October 2026. The current figures match the providers' own pages on 19 October 2026. The survey says AWS on-demand and Azure list prices were not re-verified as lower than the 2025 third-party figures.

...

## H200 and B200

The H200 is a later Hopper chip with more and faster memory, about 141 GB of HBM3e per GPU on AWS's P5e and P5en instances. The B200 is NVIDIA's Blackwell generation GPU; Lambda's page lists it with 180 GB of memory.

First-party list prices on 19 October 2026 give a clearer picture than earlier in the year:

- H200 on-demand: Runpod Secure Cloud $5.29 and Community Cloud $3.59; Nebius $5.40; CoreWeave $50.44 per 8-GPU instance, about $6.31 per GPU.
- H200 Capacity Blocks on AWS: $6.866 per GPU-hour on p5e.48xlarge and $7.895 on p5en.48xlarge, in the US regions listed.
- B200 on-demand: Lambda $6.69 per GPU on an 8-GPU instance and $6.99 for one GPU; Runpod Secure Cloud $7.99 and Community Cloud $5.98; Nebius $8.50; CoreWeave $68.80 per 8-GPU instance, about $8.60 per GPU.
- B200 Capacity Blocks on AWS: $113.666 per instance-hour, $14.208 per GPU-hour, on p6-b200.48xlarge.
- B200 clusters on Lambda: $9.86 per GPU for 16 GPUs, $9.36 for 64 and $8.87 for 256 or more, for terms of two weeks to a year.

AWS's Capacity Blocks page says its rates are updated regularly, with the next update scheduled for January 2027, and that a block is charged at the rate in effect when it is bought.

The index view is different. The Ornn Compute Price Index, reported in a post dated 27 April 2026 on tomtunguz.com, put the B200 at $4.95 per hour that week, up from $2.31 in early March, a 114% rise in six weeks. The author also reports that the B200 premium over H200 fell to $0.28 per hour in November 2025 and widened to $1.80 by late April 2026. That is one index, from one author, describing a spot style market, so its levels sit below most on-demand list prices. The takeaway is directional: Blackwell prices were rising in spring 2026, and the gap to the previous generation was widening.
